subject: Decision bridge: Brightwell VPC/on-prem constraints & operational handoff
messages:
From: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@brightwellhealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: Kevin Tran <kevin.tran@brightwellhealth.com>
Date: 2025-12-01T10:12:00Z
Subject: Redwood private hosting feasibility — Brightwell constraints

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking our request. We wanted to surface a concise list of constraints up-front so your team can evaluate feasibility quickly:

- We need a VPC/private deployment (not just multitenant) to meet our data isolation requirements.
- Data retention rules: some patient transcripts must be retained for 7 years; others must be deleted within 90 days. We'll attach the matrix.
- KMS integration: customer-managed keys required (HSM optional).
- Network: Brightwell will only allow egress with explicit allowlist and will require VPN or Direct Connect.
- Expected QPS: steady-state 50 req/s during business hours, spiky bursts up to 250 req/s for short periods.

Can you confirm whether you can support a private control plane + on-prem inference (air-gapped or restricted egress) and what the typical resourcing and timeline looks like? If helpful, we can share a short decision rubric and our compliance packet.

Appreciate a quick sanity-check so we can book a follow-up.

— Sarah
Sarah Lopez
Head of ML Platform, Brightwell Health
attachments: brightwell-data-retention-requirements.xlsx (xlsx)

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@brightwellhealth.com>, Kevin Tran <kevin.tran@brightwellhealth.com>
Date: 2025-12-01T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood private hosting feasibility — Brightwell constraints

Thanks Sarah — good context. Looping in Soojin (product), Karthik (arch/infra), and Marissa (delivery) to scope a decision bridge.

High-level asks from our side to prepare a meaningful feasibility answer:

1) Minimum acceptance criteria (we need customer to confirm):
   - Which workloads require air-gapped on-prem vs VPC with restricted egress?
   - Which data classes require "delete within 90 days" vs "retain 7 years"? (we saw the sheet but want explicit mapping to endpoints)
2) Security/compliance must-haves:
   - KMS: customer-managed key rotation windows and HSM requirement (YES/NO).
   - Audit log retention window required for compliance.
3) Traffic & SLO expectations:
   - steady QPS and allowable latency SLO (p95) for critical endpoints.
4) Network topology:
   - Will Brightwell provide a Direct Connect / ExpressRoute or require VPN only? Any constraints for NAT/egress?
5) Timeline & procurement constraints:
   - Target go-live date and procurement windows that drive decisions.

Operational note: we'll need a dedicated pilot pod for this customer if they require private control plane + on-prem inference. That has two implications: infra staffing for the pilot (1 infra SWE + 1 runtime SWE + 1 CS owner for 3 months) and a procurement/order for dedicated capacity if they want production throughput.

I propose a 60-minute decision bridge on Dec 3 to lock scope and surface a recommended delivery path (VPC-only, hybrid with on-prem inference, or fully on-prem). I've created a rough checklist (attached).

Next steps:
- Soojin & Karthik: confirm whether the runtime supports the following within our current private product footprint: HSM-backed KMS, egress allowlist enforcement, prefix/KV cache retention controls that can respect deletion policies.
- Marissa: estimate pilot resource needs and a rough timeline for an MVP.

attachment: redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf (pdf)

Thanks — Rishi

From: soojin_lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@brightwellhealth.com>
Date: 2025-12-02T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood private hosting feasibility — Brightwell constraints

SG — quick clarifications before the bridge:

- For data classes: we need the sheet mapped to endpoints. Sarah: can you add a column that names the affected API routes (e.g., /v1/generate, /v1/embeddings) and mark retention policy per route?
- KMS: we already support CMK via our private control plane, but HSM-protected keys require a supported vendor integration (we have an integration checklist). Karthik: can you confirm if that requires product changes or is configuration-only?
- Business ask: decide whether we treat this as a Managed Private customer (reserved capacity + control plane) vs an On-prem Appliance pilot — impacts billing and SLA.

I can draft the decision criteria doc ahead of the meeting if someone shares last week's SLA/price bands.

— Soojin

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Sarah Lopez <sarah.lopez@brightwellhealth.com>
Date: 2025-12-02T11:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood private hosting feasibility — Brightwell constraints

Short technical readout before bridge:

- KMS/HSM: customer-managed KMS (CMK) is configuration-only when using our private control plane in a customer's VPC. Full HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2 HSM appliance) are NOT fully automated today; we'd treat that as an integration workstream (estimated 3-4 sprints for a supported vendor integration).
- Egress control & allowlist: supported via per-pilot egress policy and firewall rules. If Brightwell requires zero external egress, we can run inference in an air-gapped mode but that requires a separate on-prem runtime package and additional ops runbook.
- Data deletion: runtime-level automatic deletion of KV cache and request logs can be implemented, but audit-proof deletion with third-party verification is a compliance ask and needs product + security sign-off.

Resource implications (rough):
- Pilot delivery: 1 infra SWE (4 wks prepilot + 8 wks pilot support on-call), 1 runtime SWE (3 sprints), 1 solutions engineer + CS rep.
- If Brightwell wants HSM integration: add 2 eng sprints and 1 security engineer for validation.

attachment: network-requirements.csv (csv)

I'll bring an arch sketch to the bridge showing isolation options (VPC private control plane vs on-prem runtime).

— Karthik

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Decision bridge: Brightwell VPC/on-prem constraints & operational handoff

Thanks all for the bridge — helpful and aligned. Short summary & decisions for tracking (to be entered in JIRA-RED-7894):

1) Scope: Brightwell will pilot with a Managed Private (VPC + private control plane) for the majority of traffic; a subset of high-risk workloads will be run on an on-prem inference runtime behind Brightwell's firewall.
2) KMS: CMK supported in VPC pilot. HSM integration is a separate workstream (add-on) — Brightwell will decide in 30 days.
3) Data retention: Brightwell will map endpoints to retention buckets and upload the finalized matrix to the Drive by Dec 10.
4) Pilot resourcing: Approved: 1 infra SWE (Karthik lead), 1 runtime SWE, 1 solutions engineer, 1 CS. Target pilot length: 12 weeks from infra readiness.
5) Network: Brightwell to confirm connectivity method (Direct Connect preferred).

Action items:
- Marissa: create pilot project in our tracker, assign resource placeholders (due 12/05).
- Karthik: post arch sketch + runbook (due 12/08).
- Soojin: draft SLA/billing treatment options & decision criteria doc (due 12/09).
- Brightwell (Sarah): finalize endpoint->retention matrix (due 12/10).

I'll follow-up with the JIRA ticket and a short one-page decision memo.

— Rishi
